summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, and a history of recurrent hyperkalemia was admitted for dizziness and leg tingling lasting 16 hours, symptoms she recognized from prior hyperkalemic episodes. In the emergency department, her potassium was 6.9 mEq/L with a normal EKG. She received standard medical treatment including insulin, dextrose, calcium gluconate, and albuterol nebs, followed by an initial hemodialysis session. She was admitted for monitoring and remained asymptomatic overnight. Morning labs showed potassium at 5.3 mEq/L, prompting a second 2.5-hour dialysis session. She recovered well, remained stable, and was discharged home with instructions to resume her regular dialysis schedule and have her potassium monitored at her next outpatient session. Her chronic medications, including warfarin and lamotrigine, were continued without change.
